land.text: Senegal, the western member of the Mali Federation (Senegal and French Sudan), whose government 'was based in Dakar, the eventual capital of Senegal'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Mali Federation shape of 1960 (1.45 M km2) holds Senegal and the Sudanese Republic together; Senegal's own row starts in 1961. Senegal had been an autonomous republic within the French Union from 25 November 1958 (Senegal page), merged with French Sudan into the Mali Federation (January 1959 on the Senegal page, 4 April 1959 on the Federation page), became independent with it on 20 June 1960 and left it on 20 August 1960.

capitals.name: Dakar
capitals.note: Infobox capital, 14°40′N 17°25′W; Dakar was also the seat of the Mali Federation's government (Mali Federation page).

correction.text: Senegal as drawn for 1961: the territory that 'declared independence from the Mali Federation at a midnight session on 20 August' 1960

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Senegal row starts in 1961, but the state exists from 20 August 1960. For 1960 Cliopatria draws one Mali Federation shape of 1,446,277 km2 (Senegal plus the Sudanese Republic); the Mali Federation dossier should end it at Senegal's secession, and Senegal's 1961 shape stands for the rest of 1960.

200,762 km2 against the infobox's 196,722 km2 (no year given), ratio 1.02: within the honest precision. The shape leaves out The Gambia (no overlap with the Gambian shape from 1967); the page records no border change after independence.

Identical to the 1961 shape; the page records no border change, name change or new republic since 1960 (the Senegambia Confederation of 1982-1989 was 'nominal' and left both states' borders as they were).

region.text: Senegal, which 'declared independence from the Mali Federation at a midnight session on 20 August'

ledger.note: 1960-08-20: Senegal declares independence from the Mali Federation. 'On 19 August 1960, Sudanese Republic leaders in the federation tried to take control by mobilizing the army'; Senegal declared independence at a midnight session on 20 August. The Senegal page agrees: the Federation, independent from France on 20 June 1960, 'broke up on 20 August 1960'. The date is the page's; the land is Cliopatria's 1961 shape, since the page names no boundary.

wars.name: Casamance conflict
belligerents: MFDC (Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance)
wars.outcome: No border change. The MFDC, 'a southern separatist group', 'has clashed sporadically with government forces since 1982'; on 30 December 2004 President Wade announced he would sign a peace treaty, but the conflict 'has not yet been fully concluded as of 2025'.
wars.note: The page names no ground the MFDC held, so no contest zone or rebel dossier is recorded; a gap-filler could open the Casamance conflict article for the extent of the rebel-held pockets.

certainty.note: Independent state within the frontiers of the French colony. The pages opened (Senegal, Mali Federation) give no boundary treaty, survey or dispute, so the level rests on the era (inherited administrative frontiers of French West Africa), not on a dated line; the river frontier with Mauritania and the enclave frontier of The Gambia are not described on them.

sources.title: Senegal
sources.note: Identity, infobox area (196,722 km2), capital Dakar, 20 June and 20 August 1960, the Senegambia Confederation (1 February 1982 to 30 September 1989), the Casamance conflict.

sources.title: Mali Federation

notes: Senegal: Cliopatria row 'Republic of Senegal' 1961..2024 (two shapes, identical), reviewed against the Senegal and Mali Federation pages (budget 1-2 pages). (1) The state is dated from its secession of 20 August 1960, not from Cliopatria's 1961; the 1960 keyframe is new and the Mali Federation row's 1960 shape (Senegal plus the Sudanese Republic) must be ended or split by the dossier of mali-federation. (2) The Senegambia Confederation (1 February 1982 to 30 September 1989: 'Senegal joined with The Gambia to form the nominal Senegambia Confederation') is an association, not territory; recorded here only in a keyframe note and proposed as an umbrella entity under counterparts_needing_dossiers. (3) The Senegal page does not describe the 1989-1991 conflict with Mauritania (it only says 40,000 Mauritanians 'were expelled from their home country in 1989'); not recorded as a war here, left to the mauritania dossier. (4) The Senegal page gives no president list; identity.rulers is omitted. (5) No gazetteer names were needed.
